chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from al-Mufadhal ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Zurarah and Humran from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
If a servant performs a deed seeking the pleasure of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the Hereafter, but includes in it the pleasure of one of the people, he is a polytheist.
ai.seo_question: What makes a good deed considered shirk in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that even a single act of worship seeking human approval alongside divine reward constitutes *shirk* in intention, not just in belief. This underscores the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) as the essential condition for the acceptance of deeds, where the purity of motive determines the spiritual validity of the action. The hadith serves as a warning against *riya* (showing off), which can invalidate otherwise correct rituals.
